# neurocenter-assets

Versioned assets for Neurocenter and the shared `@neurocenter/asset-contract` producer/consumer package. MCP servers, OpenCode plugins, skills, models, agents and the bridge keep their native installation formats.

The application flow is: provide a source → package → choose assets → import cards into the common catalog. Internal recipes, manifests and exact approval plans are generated by the server. Only genuine ambiguity or missing configuration needs a user choice. The developer commands below expose the contract; they are not a JSON-editing workflow for end users.

```sh
node bin/assets.mjs validate .
node bin/assets.mjs list .
node bin/assets.mjs preview . mcp-filesystem
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

Requires Node.js 24+. No npm install, model download, DB connection or device installation is needed for these checks. The package supports ESM and Node 24 CommonJS `require`. Neurocenter must pin an exact repository commit when consuming it.

```js
import {createToolAsset, toToolPublication} from '@neurocenter/asset-contract';
const asset = createToolAsset(preparedBuildResult);
const nativePublication = toToolPublication(asset);
// The app runs its existing publication validator before persisting/importing.
```

The existing packager calls this producer after source detection and build. `neurocenter-assets export-tool prepared-input.json new-asset.json` is its lower-level, deterministic equivalent. It refuses conflicting runtime descriptors and never overwrites an existing output.

Read the [contract](skills/neurocenter-packaging/references/contract.md), [types](index.d.ts) and [packaging skill](skills/neurocenter-packaging/SKILL.md). Index and dependency hashes always cover exact descriptor bytes, including newlines. Tools declare runtime artifacts once; the consumer derives the native card configuration automatically.

The server fetches upstream files, verifies immutable storage and imports only selected cards with provenance. Computers download through the configured **API Gateway**, with the app's existing device/project permissions, SHA checks and approved plans. Public descriptors have no deployment gateway URL or credentials. Importing a card does not install it on a computer; a remote model also needs private server configuration before use.

Five native agent templates are available for selective import: planner, developer, reviewer, tester and documenter. Their prompts come from the exact `source.commit` and `source.path` in each descriptor. Project settings pin an immutable template and can override prompts and model parameters. Enable, disable and removal are delivered to one specific workspace through the bridge; importing the card alone does not apply files or run a model.

Agent templates 1.1.0 include practical project-context discovery, source-backed replies and receipt-based system assistance. Their exact dependency closure adds three Neurocenter skills: project context, system assistance and project learning. Import resolves the source cards together; project assignment and installation still use the existing explicit workflow. A prompt cannot grant an absent MCP or filesystem capability. The npm package includes the five prompt sources and all three skill instructions. Earlier 1.0.0 templates remain immutable.

**Bridge 0.9.16 is published** with project-learning tools and a managed metadata-only collector. All seven release files passed anonymous HTTPS readback by size and SHA. Ten runtime checks passed on native macOS ARM64 and separately on Linux x64 under Docker amd64 emulation, including native OpenCode 1.14.48 collector discovery, stale-binding rejection and managed removal. The bridge suite passed 1106 tests; three explicit integration opt-ins were skipped. Dependencies were rebuilt with isolated npm configuration and verified TLS. See the [release audit](audit/bridge-0.9.16-2026-10-21.json) for exact artifacts, source provenance and execution boundaries. Existing asset versions remain unchanged.

**Bridge 0.9.15 is published** with managed project-agent delivery. All seven release files passed anonymous HTTPS readback by size and SHA. Nine runtime checks passed on native macOS ARM64 and separately on Linux x64 under Docker amd64 emulation, including compiled HTTP jobs, native OpenCode 1.14.48 discovery, enable/disable/removal and lost-ACK recovery. See the [release audit](audit/bridge-0.9.15-2026-10-21.json). Existing asset versions remain unchanged.

The five initial assets use this single source format: MCP Filesystem, Git context plugin, Qwen3 Embedding 4B, bridge 0.9.10 and the packaging skill. Their pinned release URLs are server supply locations. The earlier release files are not a second catalog or an alternate import format. Both tool archives and both bridge payloads were checked against locally available bytes; the model lock and bundle passed native metadata validation, but model download and inference were not run.

The index also includes twelve curated GitHub skills with 187 bundled resources: Vite, Vitest, PostgreSQL, NestJS, Playwright, MCP development, React state/Zustand, TypeScript, API design, accessibility, code review and CI/CD. Each preserves its pinned upstream instructions, provenance and full MIT or Apache-2.0 notice. Application owner IDs and mutable local history are excluded. Vite 8 and Vitest 5 instructions describe those majors; applicability to another major needs a separate check. Bundled scripts are documentation resources and are not executed by import.

**Python context 1.0.0 is published** with an immutable Release transport and exact byte readback. It was rebuilt from the public TypeScript example, preserving the original 1011-byte runtime SHA and a checked portable source snapshot. All eight target descriptors share that exact JavaScript archive; actual hook execution and six positive/negative filesystem cases were checked on macOS ARM64. The recipe and original source are included under `recipes/plugin-python-context/1.0.0`; [the audit](audit/python-context-2026-10-20.json) distinguishes structural targets, native execution and publication proof.

**OpenCodeRAG pack.11 is now current** for MCP and plugin delivery, with seven platform descriptors per tool and anonymous HTTPS SHA-256/size readback for all 15 release files. Every earlier descriptor remains immutable. Native macOS ARM64 checks passed MCP initialization/tool listing and plugin factory registration in disposable Seatbelt profiles; Linux/Windows runtime and full model/indexing acceptance are not claimed. See the [pack.11 audit](audit/rag-pack11-2026-10-23.json) and [release](https://github.com/ghost-raven1/neurocenter-assets/releases/tag/rag-v2.4.4-pack.11).

**Bridge 0.9.12 and OpenCodeRAG pack.9 are published** with fresh HTTPS byte readback for every archive. Bridge package metadata, MCP handshake and worker status agree; the self-contained stdio smoke passed on native macOS ARM64 and Linux x64 under Docker emulation. Version 0.9.11 was withdrawn before catalog import because it reported an inconsistent protocol version and is excluded from this index. Pack.9 keeps exact producer sources and seven platform descriptors per tool; native reindex, plugin hooks, OpenCode E2E and semantic search were exercised on macOS ARM64. Other RAG targets passed SHA, inventory, entrypoint and binary-header checks; execution on those platforms is not claimed. Previous source versions remain immutable in the index. See the [bridge audit](audit/bridge-0.9.12-2026-10-21.json) and [RAG audit](audit/rag-pack9-2026-10-21.json).

`NOASSERTION` means license clearance has not been asserted. Before redistribution, preserve and verify the upstream license and notices. The Filesystem archive's metadata refers to a LICENSE file that was not present at the expected package path; importing its descriptor does not establish permission to redistribute that archive.

For an integration check against the app's actual source validators:

```sh
node bin/check-native.mjs ../neurocenter
```

This development check needs the app's catalog/skills dependencies installed. It performs tool producer → descriptor → native publication → verified package roundtrips, checks skill resources, model locks/bundles and native bridge release metadata, and verifies remote model metadata when supported. It does not mutate catalogs, start services or run tools/models. Live protocol/platform execution and inference remain separate checks.

This repository's original code currently has no redistribution license grant (`UNLICENSED`). Making the repository public does not change upstream licenses or grant rights to third-party runtime binaries.
